title: Wrangling Telemetry at Scale: A Guide to Self-Hosted Observability
gist: Colin Douch (DuckDuckGo SRE, ex-Cloudflare observability lead) argues most teams should buy rather than self-host observability, but lays out a pragmatic open-source stack: Prometheus with exemplars, structured/canonical logs in a columnar store, OTel tracing into Jaeger/Tempo, Perses over Grafana, and a future where wide events are the single instrumentation source.

insights.claim: Self-hosting observability should be a last resort: the speaker tells most teams to stay with a provider (possibly switching away from Datadog or Splunk) and fight the urge to run their own stack.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Default to SaaS; self-host only when forced by cost, compliance or missing features.
insights.quote: do not run your own thing
insights.locator: Opening remarks

insights.claim: Legitimate triggers to self-host are bills that grow exponentially with telemetry volume, auditors questioning why so much data goes to a third party, or lacking clout with a SaaS vendor to get a needed feature.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: These are the demand drivers for open-source observability vendors; watch data-sovereignty and cost-pressure narratives.
insights.locator: There will come a time when your life starts to go downhill

insights.claim: Running a self-hosted observability stack requires at least two to three engineers just to operate it, plus more time and money than expected.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Hidden headcount cost should be netted against SaaS savings in any build-vs-buy case.
insights.quote: Be prepared to dedicate at least two to three engineers
insights.locator: Background

insights.claim: Observability is about moving between data types, not storing data, and the hardest part of building it yourself is that few open-source tools tie metrics, logs and traces together by default.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Integration glue is the gap commercial vendors monetize.
insights.locator: What Does a Self-Hosted Observability Stack Look Like?

insights.claim: VictoriaMetrics is a better pure time-series database on efficiency, scalability and ease of running, but Prometheus wins for observability because it supports exemplars, which VictoriaMetrics refused to implement.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Exemplar support is the tie-breaker for correlation workflows; VictoriaMetrics' gap is a competitive weakness.
insights.locator: Metrics

insights.claim: Exemplars attach a changing second labelset such as a trace ID to a metric, letting Grafana show them on graphs for one-click jumps from a metric spike to the explaining traces.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: The mechanism that stitches metrics to traces and logs.
insights.locator: What exemplars allow you to do

insights.claim: Prometheus does not scale horizontally; it buffers the last two hours of series in memory as the head chunk, which Cloudflare found costs about 4 KB per active time series, a figure to use for capacity planning.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete sizing rule; memory-bound head chunks drive the move to remote-write systems.
insights.locator: For your active time series

insights.claim: Mimir and Cortex use remote write to remove the head-chunk limit, while Thanos uploads only completed two-hour blocks and pulls from sidecars, making highly distributed environments harder, though its distributed query engine pushes computation down to sidecars.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Choose Mimir/Cortex for head-chunk pain and Thanos for many-datacenter query pushdown.
insights.locator: Mimir and Cortex, through Prometheus's remote write system

insights.claim: Thanos is experimenting with rewriting Prometheus blocks into Parquet, with benchmarks reaching roughly VictoriaMetrics-level performance without its micro-optimizations; it remains an experiment.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: If upstreamed, it could erode VictoriaMetrics' performance advantage inside the Prometheus ecosystem.
insights.locator: The other is the Parquet storage engine

insights.claim: Plain-text logs and full-text search degrade at scale (searching user 20 also matches 202 and 2070), so structured logs in a store that indexes fields with dynamic schemas are required.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Unstructured log search is a cost and accuracy dead end.
insights.locator: The simplest example I can give is searching for user records

insights.claim: Elasticsearch handles dynamic fields poorly: ingestion halts past a dynamic-field limit, and raising the limit too high tanks performance.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Pushes log workloads toward columnar engines.
insights.locator: Dynamic field support in Elasticsearch just sucks

insights.claim: Grafana Loki indexes only stream labels chosen at ingest, so anything else falls back to full-text search, which the speaker calls not very observability; VictoriaLogs, a full columnar database, lacks that limitation and is his recommendation for new or migrating setups.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Columnar log stores with dynamic indexing are gaining ground against Loki's label model.
insights.locator: The first real competitor to come out was Loki

insights.claim: Inserting logs directly into ClickHouse works but is higher maintenance; Cloudflare managed it only because it had a dedicated ClickHouse team, so it is not worth starting just for logging.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: ClickHouse operational burden favors packaged log stores for most teams.
insights.locator: Of course, you could just go with a dedicated columnar database

insights.claim: Canonical logging, credited to Stripe, accumulates fields in a context block through a unit of work and emits one wide log per block at the end, bridging logging and tracing and carrying a correlation ID usable for exemplars.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: One wide event per request simplifies debugging and is the base for the wide-events future.
insights.locator: What we really need is a way to tie all of those logs together

insights.claim: A trace is just structured logs with span IDs, a trace ID and a parent span ID; the parent-child link gives causal ordering that timestamps cannot, since time on computers can go backwards.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Explains why tracing adds value beyond logs.
insights.quote: Anything else is just sparkling logs
insights.locator: Tracing

insights.claim: The speaker recommends OTel libraries for tracing only, calling them the most stable telemetry type, and advises against OTel's metrics and logs specs, which he says ignore existing communities like Prometheus; Jaeger and Zipkin instrumentation are deprecated in favour of OTel.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: OTel is the de facto tracing standard but contested on metrics/logs, a friction point for vendor-neutral stacks.
insights.locator: Because tracing has become this hot buzzword

insights.claim: Tempo wins on actionable features (TraceQL, metrics from traces) but its own storage engine reportedly does not scale beyond tens of thousands of traces per second; Jaeger is storage-agnostic and scales, which is why Cloudflare used it, though Cloudflare built missing features in a private fork.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: No open-source tracer is both feature-rich and scalable, an opening for new entrants.
insights.locator: Yet again, we have a few options here, mostly Jaeger or Tempo

insights.claim: The lack of a fully featured scalable open-source tracing system is called one of the biggest downsides of open-source observability; VictoriaTraces is on the way but too new to trust.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Watch VictoriaTraces and HyperDX as potential gap-fillers.
insights.locator: I really think there's an opportunity here for Jaeger to improve

insights.claim: Head sampling is simple but requires embedding the sampling rate in each span so query-time multipliers are right; tail sampling needs trace buffering and sharding and is recommended against unless head sampling's problems are hit, or above tens of thousands of spans per second.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Sampling strategy drives cost and complexity; default to head sampling.
insights.locator: We should probably talk about sampling

insights.claim: The OTel Collector is described, by a contributor, as a bit of a mess: CNCF bureaucracy and unpaid volunteers make even minor changes take weeks, forcing internal forks for timely changes, so he cannot yet recommend running it. Alternatives are Grafana Alloy and Vector, which was recently acquired by Datadog.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Telemetry pipeline tooling is immature and consolidating; Datadog owning Vector is a vendor-neutrality risk.
insights.locator: Again, a few options here

insights.claim: Perses, a CNCF project, is proposed over Grafana because Grafana locks useful features such as dashboard usage tracking and data-source permissions behind paid tiers and rejects upstream contributions, while Perses offers them plus ephemeral dashboards.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Open-core friction creates room for Perses; watch adoption.
insights.locator: UI - Tying It All Together

insights.claim: Dashboards should be tagged as long-lived BI dashboards or debugging dashboards, with debugging ones audited for deletion, since each incident differs and they accumulate as copies of copies.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Dashboard sprawl is a hidden maintenance cost.
insights.locator: You have your BI dashboards

insights.claim: Metrics, logs and traces are the same data at different granularities, so with sufficiently wide high-context events instrumented once, the other signals can be derived by the observability tool; the three pillars get pushed up the stack rather than disappearing.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Single-instrumentation wide-event architectures could commoditize separate metrics/logs/traces products.
insights.locator: What About the Future?

insights.claim: SigNoz is cited as an ok all-in-one solution that suffers from doing everything fine and nothing great.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: All-in-one open-source stacks are not yet best-of-breed.
insights.quote: doing everything fine and nothing great
insights.locator: What About the Future?

insights.claim: AI observability today amounts to dumping traces into a context window, and wide events burn context quickly, so an intermediate layer must distil information before it reaches an AI agent; pointing an MCP server straight at a logging API risks hallucination.
insights.speaker: Colin Douch
insights.so_what: Opportunity for telemetry summarization layers; naive AI-SRE integrations will underperform.
insights.locator: Questions and Answers
